interpretations.explanation: 2019-01-13. Sinus bradycardia, rate 53 (RR 1112-1170 ms, regular), upright consistent P waves in II/aVF preceded each QRS with PR 138 ms. QRS 94 ms with a qR pattern in I/V5-V6 and deep S in III/aVF; frontal axis about -14 deg (normal). QT 382 ms, Bazett QTc 358 ms. No bundle branch block or AV block. Versus the prior tracing of 2018-12-13 (sinus 66, PR 152, QRS 110, QTc 385) the QRS is now narrower and the QTc essentially unchanged (-27 ms); neither study met bundle-branch-block criteria, so no change is coded.

2023-10-08. Sinus rhythm, rate 68 (RR 862-902 ms), upright P in II/aVF, PR 136 ms. QRS 94 ms, rS in V1-V2 with tall R in V5-V6, frontal axis +44 deg (normal). Repolarisation is clearly prolonged: QT 488 ms with Bazett QTc 520 ms - above the 500 ms clinic threshold in a patient on escitalopram. No bundle branch block or AV block. Compared with 2022-11-23 (100065910: sinus 76, PR 146, QRS 92, QTc 361) the QTc has increased by about 159 ms: QTC_INCREASE_60.

2023-11-10. Sinus rhythm, rate 70 (RR 798-886 ms), upright P waves in II/III/aVF, PR 154 ms. QRS 104 ms - mildly widened but without a bundle branch block pattern (rS in V1, no broad terminal R, no broad monophasic R in I/V6). Frontal axis +52 deg (normal). Greatly prolonged repolarisation with a broad flat T wave: QT 506 ms, Bazett QTc 548 ms, well above the 500 ms threshold on citalopram 40 mg. Compared with 2020-06-17 (107149156: sinus tachycardia 132, QRS 78, QTc about 426 ms) the QTc has risen by over 100 ms: QTC_INCREASE_60.

2024-04-19. Sinus tachycardia, rate 121 (RR 476-514 ms). A low-amplitude but consistent upright P wave (0.06-0.08 mV in II/III/aVF, negative in V1) precedes each QRS with PR about 136 ms. QRS 82 ms, rS in V1-V2 with tall R in V5-V6, frontal axis +63 deg (normal). QT 286 ms, QTc 406 ms. No bundle branch block or AV block. This is the only ECG on file, so there is no prior tracing for comparison.

2024-05-21. Sinus tachycardia, rate 108 (RR 546-616 ms), upright P waves in II/aVF, PR 116 ms. QRS 92 ms with an rS in V1-V2, R/S transition at V2-V3 and a moderate R in V5-V6; frontal axis +46 deg (normal). QT about 326 ms, QTc about 438 ms. No bundle branch block or AV block. Only ECG on file - no prior study for comparison.

2024-05-23. Sinus rhythm at 98 (RR 614-628 ms, regular), upright P in II/III/aVF with a short PR of 94 ms. Narrow QRS 76 ms; tall R in I and V5 (2.0 mV) with deep rS in V1-V2 and an rS in III, giving a frontal axis of about +4 deg (normal). QT 306 ms, QTc 390 ms. No bundle branch block or AV block. Only ECG on file - no prior study for comparison.

2024-07-17. Sinus rhythm, rate 59 (RR 954-1154 ms) with an upright P in II/aVF and a prolonged PR of 208 ms - first-degree AV block. QRS is broad at 134 ms with a left bundle branch block pattern: broad monophasic R in I (peak 24 ms, no S) and in V6, deep broad QS complexes in V1-V2 and III, and delayed intrinsicoid deflection; frontal axis about -28 deg. QT 430 ms, QTc 427 ms. Compared with 2024-06-03 (103686933) the same 132 ms LBBB pattern was already present with QTc 438 ms, so no new or resolved bundle branch block and no significant QTc change; the PR has lengthened from 124 to 208 ms.

2024-09-17. Atrial fibrillation: no P waves in any lead (pre-QRS baseline flat at the noise level) and a grossly irregularly irregular ventricular response, RR 410-912 ms, mean rate 103. PR interval not measurable. QRS 86 ms with a small r and deep S in II/III/aVF and tall R in I/V5, frontal axis about -53 deg (left axis deviation). QT 316 ms, QTc 413 ms. No bundle branch block. Only ECG on file, so no prior tracing for comparison; the patient is on warfarin.

2024-10-24. Sinus bradycardia, rate 52 and very regular (RR 1144-1178 ms, CV 0.009). A low-amplitude (about 0.06 mV) but reproducible upright P wave in II/III/aVF precedes each QRS, PR about 150 ms - no fibrillatory activity despite the history of atrial fibrillation. QRS 96 ms with very tall R waves in V5-V6 (4.1/3.3 mV) and deep S in V1-V2; frontal axis +37 deg (normal). QT 436 ms, QTc 404 ms. No bundle branch block or AV block. Versus 2023-05-22 (104629882: sinus 58 with one premature beat, PR 142, QRS 92, QTc 387) there is no significant change.

2024-11-15. Atrial fibrillation: no organised P waves (pre-QRS signal at baseline, no reproducible atrial deflection across beats) with a grossly irregular ventricular response, RR 454-1148 ms, mean rate 70. PR not measurable. QRS 100 ms with terminal slurring but no complete bundle branch block pattern; tall R in I/V5-V6, deep S in V1-V2; frontal axis +30 deg (normal). QT 430 ms, QTc 466 ms. Compared with the tracing three days earlier (107873952, 2024-11-12) which showed sinus rhythm at 69 with clear P waves, PR 160 ms, QRS 86 ms and QTc 388 ms, this is NEW_AF, and the QTc has risen by about 78 ms (QTC_INCREASE_60).

2024-12-05 14:38. Sinus tachycardia, rate 122 and metronomically regular (RR 492-496 ms), small upright P waves in II/aVF, PR 124 ms. QRS has narrowed to 86 ms. Overall QRS voltage is low; lead I is net negative and aVF near isoelectric, giving a rightward/indeterminate frontal axis of roughly +163 deg (RIGHT). QT 300 ms, QTc 427 ms. Compared with the tracing from earlier the same day (106516875, 01:33) which showed a 144 ms right bundle branch block - tall broad terminal R in V1 peaking at 62 ms with wide S waves in I and V6 - the QRS is now narrow: RESOLVED_BUNDLE_BRANCH_BLOCK. QTc fell from 468 to 427 ms (less than 60 ms).

2020-06-19. Sinus rhythm, rate 76 (RR 774-804 ms), prominent upright P waves in II/III/aVF (0.21 mV) with PR 154 ms. Narrow QRS 72 ms, rS in V1 with normal precordial progression, frontal axis +66 deg (normal). QT 396 ms, QTc 447 ms. No conduction block. Compared with 2020-02-02 (109048192: sinus 75, PR 154, QRS 64, QTc 529 ms with diffuse low-amplitude T-wave inversion) the repolarisation has largely normalised: QTc fell by about 82 ms, coded QTC_DECREASE_60.

2025-02-15. Sinus rhythm, rate 74 and regular (RR 802-824 ms), P wave upright in I and II (negative in III) with PR 174 ms. QRS 90 ms with large biphasic complexes in the limb leads (I +1.25/-0.82 mV, III +1.20/-1.13 mV); net frontal axis about +37 deg (normal). QT 378 ms, QTc 420 ms. No bundle branch block or AV block. Only ECG on file - no prior study for comparison.

2025-03-09. Sinus bradycardia, rate 58 (RR 976-1082 ms), tall upright P waves in II/III/aVF (0.17 mV) with PR 110 ms. QRS 90 ms with deep rS in V1-V2 (V2 S 3.0 mV) and tall R in V5-V6; frontal axis +60 deg (normal). QT 408 ms, QTc 403 ms. No bundle branch block or AV block - a useful baseline now that haloperidol has been started. Versus the previous day (106045460, 2025-03-08: sinus 62, PR 110, QRS 92, QTc 436) there is no significant change.

2025-03-14. Sinus rhythm at 62 with an isolated premature atrial beat: RR are 956-986 ms apart from one early cycle of 548 ms followed by a 1202 ms pause. A discrete P wave (upright in I, low in II, negative in III) precedes each sinus QRS with PR 198 ms, at the upper limit of normal but not yet first-degree AV block. QRS 104 ms, tall R in I and V5 with rS in II/III/aVF; net frontal axis about -26 deg (borderline leftward but within the normal range). QT 368 ms, QTc 374 ms. No bundle branch block. No P-wave-less irregular activity - no atrial fibrillation on this tracing, although paroxysmal AF is documented. Only ECG on file - no prior study for comparison.

2021-01-18. Sinus tachycardia, rate 121 and strikingly regular (RR 496-500 ms). A discrete upright P wave (0.19 mV in II, negative in V1) sits between the previous T wave and the QRS, giving PR about 175 ms. QRS 88 ms, rS in V1-V2 with tall R in V5, frontal axis +44 deg (normal). QT 276 ms, QTc 391 ms. No bundle branch block. Versus 2016-09-16 (sinus tachycardia 108, PR 176, QRS 88, QTc 397) there is no significant change.

2021-08-23 10:07. Sinus rhythm at the upper limit of normal, rate 102 (RR 586-608 ms), upright P in II/aVF, PR 138 ms. QRS 94 ms with deep rS in V1-V2 and tall R in V5-V6 (voltage suggesting LV hypertrophy), frontal axis +56 deg (normal). QT 316 ms, QTc 411 ms. No bundle branch block or AV block. Essentially identical to the tracing taken one minute earlier the same day (102910502: rate 100, PR 138, QRS 94, QTc 408) - no change.

2022-04-27. Sinus bradycardia, rate 58 with only gradual RR variation (972-1098 ms) and a small but consistent P wave (about 0.05 mV, best seen in I/aVF) before every QRS, PR 166 ms. QRS 88 ms, rS V1-V2 with tall R in V5-V6, frontal axis +25 deg (normal). Markedly prolonged repolarisation: QT 542 ms, Bazett QTc 532 ms - relevant on amiodarone plus warfarin. No bundle branch block. Compared with 2022-04-06 (100867733), which showed atrial fibrillation with no P waves and a grossly irregular response at a mean 129 bpm, organised atrial activity has returned (RESOLVED_AF) and the QTc has risen by about 96 ms (QTC_INCREASE_60).

2022-05-01. Sinus tachycardia, rate 107 (RR 542-576 ms, regular). A separate upright P wave follows the T wave in each cycle (0.18 mV in II), PR about 150 ms. QRS narrow at 68 ms, deep S in V1-V2 with tall R in V5, frontal axis +52 deg (normal). QT about 336 ms, QTc about 450 ms. No conduction block. Versus 2019-07-27 (sinus 75, PR 150, QRS 86, QTc 427) there is no significant change apart from the faster rate.

2022-07-13. Sinus tachycardia, rate 141 and regular (RR 404-454 ms, CV 0.02). A small discrete P wave (0.05 mV in II, 0.11 mV in V1) is visible after the T wave in each cycle, PR about 106 ms. QRS 84 ms with tall R in I, rS in III and very deep S in V1-V2, frontal axis about -3 deg (normal). QT about 274 ms, QTc about 420 ms. No bundle branch block. The previous tracing two days earlier (109839112, 2022-07-11) showed atrial fibrillation - absent P waves with RR 382-822 ms - so sinus rhythm has been restored: RESOLVED_AF. QTc unchanged (425 to 420 ms).

2022-07-16. Sinus rhythm, rate 91 and very regular (RR 652-666 ms), upright P waves in II/aVF with PR 158 ms. QRS 84 ms; rS in III and aVF with an isoelectric net lead II, giving a frontal axis of about -18 deg (within the normal -30 to +90 range but leftward). Prominent R in V5-V6 with deep S in V1-V2. QT 334 ms, QTc 412 ms. No bundle branch block or AV block. Versus 2021-05-16 (sinus 87, PR 136, QRS 86, QTc 396) only a modest leftward axis shift; no coded change.

2023-06-26. Sinus tachycardia, rate 112 (RR 506-572 ms). One upright P wave per cycle (0.15 mV in II, positive in III/aVF, biphasic in V1) clearly separated from the preceding T wave, PR about 170 ms - there is no sawtooth flutter activity despite the history of atrial flutter. QRS 92 ms with a very deep S in V1-V2 (up to 4.8 mV) and tall R in V5-V6, frontal axis +40 deg (normal). QT 286 ms, QTc 390 ms. No bundle branch block. Versus 2022-07-04 (sinus tachycardia 115, PR 160, QRS 90, QTc 390) the tracings are essentially identical - no change.

arguments.explanation: 2025-03-19. Sinus rhythm at 102 (RR 580-594 ms, regular), upright P in II with PR 130 ms. QRS 92 ms, small R in V1 with tall R in V5-V6, frontal axis +44 deg (normal). ECG 106885519 was recorded 2025-11-24, 14 days after the start, so the requirement was met.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch list) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-02-12 (first escitalopram order; newly listed in that note). Started before 3/1/2026, so the 9/1/2025 memo 30-day window applies: ECG due by 2026-03-14. ECG 101538691 was recorded 2026-03-08, 24 days after the start, within the window - requirement met (QTc 437 ms, acceptable).

Citalopram 40 mg daily (QT watch list) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-03-02 (first citalopram order; newly listed in that note). Start is on/after 3/1/2026, so the revised memo applies with a 14-day window: ECG due by 2026-03-16. ECG 104882441 was recorded at the 2026-03-07 clinic visit, 5 days after the start - requirement met (QTc 381 ms).

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch list) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-04-10 (first escitalopram order; newly listed in that note). Start on/after 3/1/2026, so a 14-day window applies: ECG due by 2026-04-24. The only ECG on file (107859369) was recorded 2026-04-29, five days after the deadline, so nothing satisfied the requirement within the required time and the due date has passed - overdue.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch list) was restarted at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-08-01 - it appears newly in that note current-medication list and the only prior exposure was a brief inpatient surgical course 2025-12-30 to 2026-01-01, seven months earlier. Start on/after 3/1/2026, so a 14-day window applies: ECG due by 2026-08-15. No ECG has been recorded since 2025-12-25 (106035722) and the due date has passed - overdue.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch list) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-08-10 (newly listed in that note; no prior escitalopram). Start on/after 3/1/2026, so a 14-day window applies: ECG due by 2026-08-24. The nurse telephone note of 2026-08-25 records that the patient had an ECG at Northside Urgent Care on 8/18/2026 - inside the window - and that the report was requested by fax but not yet received. That outside tracing could have satisfied the requirement but it is not in the chart, so completion cannot be determined; the report should be chased.

Haloperidol 2 mg twice daily (QT watch list) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-09-15 (newly listed in that note; no prior haloperidol order). Start on/after 3/1/2026, so a 14-day window applies: ECG due by 2026-09-29. No ECG has been obtained since 2025-03-09, but as of the 2026-09-24 evaluation the requirement is not yet due.

Warfarin dose change made by a Cardiology Clinic clinician (Dr. Paul Kessler) in the 2026-09-01 clinic note: INR today 1.6, subtherapeutic. Increase warfarin to 7.5 mg daily; recheck INR. Under the 3/1/2026 memo an INR is required within 7 days, i.e. by 2026-09-08. INR 2.3 was resulted on 2026-09-05, four days after the change - requirement met.

Warfarin dose change made by a clinic pharmacist acting under the anticoagulation standing order (L. Nguyen, PharmD, 2026-09-10 anticoagulation clinic telephone note): home INR 3.4, warfarin decreased from 5 mg to 4 mg daily per protocol. The 3/1/2026 memo requires an INR within 7 days, i.e. by 2026-09-17. The home INR 3.4 is the result that prompted the change, not a follow-up, and no INR has been resulted since 2026-08-22 (2.6). The due date has passed with no confirmatory INR - overdue.

71-year-old man with atrial fibrillation (Condition ICD-9 427.31, carried in every cardiology clinic note through 2026-07-28) and no anticoagulant current: the only active outpatient order is tamsulosin (2026-07-28 to 2027-01-01) and the 2026-07-28 note lists tamsulosin alone. CHA2DS2-VASc 3 (hypertension 1, age 71 -> 1, vascular disease 1 - coronary atherosclerosis of native coronary artery with three-vessel CABG plus LIMA graft on 2025-08-22). Score >=2 in a man: guideline recommends oral anticoagulation. Note the documented peri-procedural haemorrhage (ICD-9 998.11) from that admission should be weighed at review.

Apixaban 5 mg twice daily is current (order 2026-08-20 through 2026-12-28, and the 2026-08-20 clinic note lists apixaban under Continue current regimen). However the 2026-08-12 summary-of-episode note documents an outside admission 8/2-8/5/2026 for upper GI bleeding from a duodenal ulcer, haemoglobin nadir 6.9 g/dL, 2 units transfused, with apixaban HELD at discharge pending cardiology review. The anticoagulant was restarted without that review being documented, and the patient is also on aspirin 81 mg and clopidogrel 75 mg, compounding bleeding risk. Needs prescriber review before continuing.

Two different oral anticoagulants are simultaneously current: apixaban 5 mg twice daily (order 2026-07-15 to 2026-12-26) and rivaroxaban 20 mg daily (order 2026-07-15 to 2026-12-25). The 2026-07-15 cardiology note states the intention was to switch FROM rivaroxaban TO apixaban for insurance coverage, but the rivaroxaban order was never stopped and the same note still lists both agents as current medications. Overlapping factor Xa inhibitors greatly increase bleeding risk, particularly with concurrent CLL; one order must be discontinued.

The 2026-06-10 cardiology clinic note states ECG obtained today: normal sinus rhythm, rate 72. Both ECGs recorded that day (107914094 at 17:13 and 103088543 at 19:36) show atrial fibrillation with a rapid, grossly irregular ventricular response: no P waves at all in any lead, RR intervals ranging 346-718 ms (mean rate 134-136 bpm). The documented rhythm and rate are contradicted by the same-day tracings, and a rate of ~135 in AF on warfarin needs rate-control review.

interpretations.explanation: 2019-01-13. Sinus bradycardia, rate 53 (RR 1112-1170 ms, regular), upright consistent P waves in II/aVF preceded each QRS with PR 138 ms. QRS 94 ms with a qR pattern in I/V5-V6 and deep S in III/aVF; frontal axis about -14 deg (normal). QT 382 ms, Bazett QTc 358 ms. No bundle branch block or AV block. Versus the prior tracing of 2018-12-13 (sinus 66, PR 152, QRS 110, QTc 385) the QRS is now narrower and the QTc essentially unchanged (-27 ms); neither study met bundle-branch-block criteria, so no change is coded.

2023-10-08. Sinus rhythm, rate 68 (RR 862-902 ms), upright P in II/aVF, PR 136 ms. QRS 94 ms, rS in V1-V2 with tall R in V5-V6, frontal axis +44 deg (normal). Repolarisation is clearly prolonged: QT 488 ms with Bazett QTc 520 ms - above the 500 ms clinic threshold in a patient on escitalopram. No bundle branch block or AV block. Compared with 2022-11-23 (100065910: sinus 76, PR 146, QRS 92, QTc 361) the QTc has increased by about 159 ms: QTC_INCREASE_60.

2023-11-10. Sinus rhythm, rate 70 (RR 798-886 ms), upright P waves in II/III/aVF, PR 154 ms. QRS 104 ms - mildly widened but without a bundle branch block pattern (rS in V1, no broad terminal R, no broad monophasic R in I/V6). Frontal axis +52 deg (normal). Greatly prolonged repolarisation with a broad flat T wave: QT 506 ms, Bazett QTc 548 ms, well above the 500 ms threshold on citalopram 40 mg. Compared with 2020-06-17 (107149156: sinus tachycardia 132, QRS 78, QTc about 426 ms) the QTc has risen by over 100 ms: QTC_INCREASE_60.

2024-04-19. Sinus tachycardia, rate 121 (RR 476-514 ms). A low-amplitude but consistent upright P wave (0.06-0.08 mV in II/III/aVF, negative in V1) precedes each QRS with PR about 136 ms. QRS 82 ms, rS in V1-V2 with tall R in V5-V6, frontal axis +63 deg (normal). QT 286 ms, QTc 406 ms. No bundle branch block or AV block. This is the only ECG on file, so there is no prior tracing for comparison.

2024-05-21. Sinus tachycardia, rate 108 (RR 546-616 ms), upright P waves in II/aVF, PR 116 ms. QRS 92 ms with an rS in V1-V2, R/S transition at V2-V3 and a moderate R in V5-V6; frontal axis +46 deg (normal). QT about 326 ms, QTc about 438 ms. No bundle branch block or AV block. Only ECG on file - no prior study for comparison.

2024-05-23. Sinus rhythm at 98 (RR 614-628 ms, regular), upright P in II/III/aVF with a short PR of 94 ms. Narrow QRS 76 ms; tall R in I and V5 (2.0 mV) with deep rS in V1-V2 and an rS in III, giving a frontal axis of about +4 deg (normal). QT 306 ms, QTc 390 ms. No bundle branch block or AV block. Only ECG on file - no prior study for comparison.

2024-07-17. Sinus rhythm, rate 59 (RR 954-1154 ms) with an upright P in II/aVF and a prolonged PR of 208 ms - first-degree AV block. QRS is broad at 134 ms with a left bundle branch block pattern: broad monophasic R in I (peak 24 ms, no S) and in V6, deep broad QS complexes in V1-V2 and III, and delayed intrinsicoid deflection; frontal axis about -28 deg. QT 430 ms, QTc 427 ms. Compared with 2024-06-03 (103686933) the same 132 ms LBBB pattern was already present with QTc 438 ms, so no new or resolved bundle branch block and no significant QTc change; the PR has lengthened from 124 to 208 ms.

2024-09-17. Atrial fibrillation: no P waves in any lead (pre-QRS baseline flat at the noise level) and a grossly irregularly irregular ventricular response, RR 410-912 ms, mean rate 103. PR interval not measurable. QRS 86 ms with a small r and deep S in II/III/aVF and tall R in I/V5, frontal axis about -53 deg (left axis deviation). QT 316 ms, QTc 413 ms. No bundle branch block. Only ECG on file, so no prior tracing for comparison; the patient is on warfarin.

2024-10-24. Sinus bradycardia, rate 52 and very regular (RR 1144-1178 ms, CV 0.009). A low-amplitude (about 0.06 mV) but reproducible upright P wave in II/III/aVF precedes each QRS, PR about 150 ms - no fibrillatory activity despite the history of atrial fibrillation. QRS 96 ms with very tall R waves in V5-V6 (4.1/3.3 mV) and deep S in V1-V2; frontal axis +37 deg (normal). QT 436 ms, QTc 404 ms. No bundle branch block or AV block. Versus 2023-05-22 (104629882: sinus 58 with one premature beat, PR 142, QRS 92, QTc 387) there is no significant change.

2024-11-15. Atrial fibrillation: no organised P waves (pre-QRS signal at baseline, no reproducible atrial deflection across beats) with a grossly irregular ventricular response, RR 454-1148 ms, mean rate 70. PR not measurable. QRS 100 ms with terminal slurring but no complete bundle branch block pattern; tall R in I/V5-V6, deep S in V1-V2; frontal axis +30 deg (normal). QT 430 ms, QTc 466 ms. Compared with the tracing three days earlier (107873952, 2024-11-12) which showed sinus rhythm at 69 with clear P waves, PR 160 ms, QRS 86 ms and QTc 388 ms, this is NEW_AF, and the QTc has risen by about 78 ms (QTC_INCREASE_60).

2024-12-05 14:38. Sinus tachycardia, rate 122 and metronomically regular (RR 492-496 ms), small upright P waves in II/aVF, PR 124 ms. QRS has narrowed to 86 ms. Overall QRS voltage is low; lead I is net negative and aVF near isoelectric, giving a rightward/indeterminate frontal axis of roughly +163 deg (RIGHT). QT 300 ms, QTc 427 ms. Compared with the tracing from earlier the same day (106516875, 01:33) which showed a 144 ms right bundle branch block - tall broad terminal R in V1 peaking at 62 ms with wide S waves in I and V6 - the QRS is now narrow: RESOLVED_BUNDLE_BRANCH_BLOCK. QTc fell from 468 to 427 ms (less than 60 ms).

2020-06-19. Sinus rhythm, rate 76 (RR 774-804 ms), prominent upright P waves in II/III/aVF (0.21 mV) with PR 154 ms. Narrow QRS 72 ms, rS in V1 with normal precordial progression, frontal axis +66 deg (normal). QT 396 ms, QTc 447 ms. No conduction block. Compared with 2020-02-02 (109048192: sinus 75, PR 154, QRS 64, QTc 529 ms with diffuse low-amplitude T-wave inversion) the repolarisation has largely normalised: QTc fell by about 82 ms, coded QTC_DECREASE_60.

2025-02-15. Sinus rhythm, rate 74 and regular (RR 802-824 ms), P wave upright in I and II (negative in III) with PR 174 ms. QRS 90 ms with large biphasic complexes in the limb leads (I +1.25/-0.82 mV, III +1.20/-1.13 mV); net frontal axis about +37 deg (normal). QT 378 ms, QTc 420 ms. No bundle branch block or AV block. Only ECG on file - no prior study for comparison.

2025-03-09. Sinus bradycardia, rate 58 (RR 976-1082 ms), tall upright P waves in II/III/aVF (0.17 mV) with PR 110 ms. Versus the previous day (106045460, 2025-03-08: sinus 62, PR 110, QRS 92, QTc 436) there is no significant change.

A discrete P wave (upright in I, low in II, negative in III) precedes each sinus QRS with PR 198 ms, at the upper limit of normal but not yet first-degree AV block. QRS 104 ms, tall R in I and V5 with rS in II/III/aVF; net frontal axis about -26 deg (borderline leftward but within the normal range). QT 368 ms, QTc 374 ms. No bundle branch block. No P-wave-less irregular activity - no atrial fibrillation on this tracing, although paroxysmal AF is documented. Only ECG on file - no prior study for comparison.

2025-03-19. Sinus rhythm at 102 (RR 580-594 ms, regular), upright P in II with PR 130 ms. QRS 92 ms, small R in V1 with tall R in V5-V6, frontal axis +44 deg (normal). QT 326 ms, QTc 425 ms. No bundle branch block or AV block. Versus the previous day (101016166, 2025-03-18: sinus 102, PR 128, QRS 92, QTc 421) there is no change.

2025-05-12. Sinus rhythm, rate 82 and regular (RR 710-744 ms), upright P in I/II/aVF, PR 132 ms. QRS mildly widened at 106 ms with nonspecific terminal slurring but no bundle branch block pattern (rS in V1, no broad monophasic R in I/V6, no terminal R in V1). Frontal axis about +28 deg (normal). QT 372 ms, QTc 436 ms. No AV block. Only ECG on file - no prior study for comparison.

2021-01-18. Sinus tachycardia, rate 121 and strikingly regular (RR 496-500 ms). A discrete upright P wave (0.19 mV in II, negative in V1) sits between the previous T wave and the QRS, giving PR about 175 ms. QRS 88 ms, rS in V1-V2 with tall R in V5, frontal axis +44 deg (normal). QT 276 ms, QTc 391 ms. No bundle branch block. Versus 2016-09-16 (sinus tachycardia 108, PR 176, QRS 88, QTc 397) there is no significant change.

2021-08-23 10:07. Sinus rhythm at the upper limit of normal, rate 102 (RR 586-608 ms), upright P in II/aVF, PR 138 ms. QRS 94 ms with deep rS in V1-V2 and tall R in V5-V6 (voltage suggesting LV hypertrophy), frontal axis +56 deg (normal). QT 316 ms, QTc 411 ms. No bundle branch block or AV block. Essentially identical to the tracing taken one minute earlier the same day (102910502: rate 100, PR 138, QRS 94, QTc 408) - no change.

2022-04-27. Sinus bradycardia, rate 58 with only gradual RR variation (972-1098 ms) and a small but consistent P wave (about 0.05 mV, best seen in I/aVF) before every QRS, PR 166 ms. QRS 88 ms, rS V1-V2 with tall R in V5-V6, frontal axis +25 deg (normal). Markedly prolonged repolarisation: QT 542 ms, Bazett QTc 532 ms - relevant on amiodarone plus warfarin. No bundle branch block. Compared with 2022-04-06 (100867733), which showed atrial fibrillation with no P waves and a grossly irregular response at a mean 129 bpm, organised atrial activity has returned (RESOLVED_AF) and the QTc has risen by about 96 ms (QTC_INCREASE_60).

2022-05-01. Sinus tachycardia, rate 107 (RR 542-576 ms, regular). A separate upright P wave follows the T wave in each cycle (0.18 mV in II), PR about 150 ms. QRS narrow at 68 ms, deep S in V1-V2 with tall R in V5, frontal axis +52 deg (normal). QT about 336 ms, QTc about 450 ms. No conduction block. Versus 2019-07-27 (sinus 75, PR 150, QRS 86, QTc 427) there is no significant change apart from the faster rate.

2022-07-13. Sinus tachycardia, rate 141 and regular (RR 404-454 ms, CV 0.02). A small discrete P wave (0.05 mV in II, 0.11 mV in V1) is visible after the T wave in each cycle, PR about 106 ms. QRS 84 ms with tall R in I, rS in III and very deep S in V1-V2, frontal axis about -3 deg (normal). QT about 274 ms, QTc about 420 ms. No bundle branch block. The previous tracing two days earlier (109839112, 2022-07-11) showed atrial fibrillation - absent P waves with RR 382-822 ms - so sinus rhythm has been restored: RESOLVED_AF. QTc unchanged (425 to 420 ms).

2022-07-16. Sinus rhythm, rate 91 and very regular (RR 652-666 ms), upright P waves in II/aVF with PR 158 ms. QRS 84 ms; rS in III and aVF with an isoelectric net lead II, giving a frontal axis of about -18 deg (within the normal -30 to +90 range but leftward). Prominent R in V5-V6 with deep S in V1-V2. QT 334 ms, QTc 412 ms. No bundle branch block or AV block. Versus 2021-05-16 (sinus 87, PR 136, QRS 86, QTc 396) only a modest leftward axis shift; no coded change.

2023-06-26. Sinus tachycardia, rate 112 (RR 506-572 ms). One upright P wave per cycle (0.15 mV in II, positive in III/aVF, biphasic in V1) clearly separated from the preceding T wave, PR about 170 ms - there is no sawtooth flutter activity despite the history of atrial flutter. QRS 92 ms with a very deep S in V1-V2 (up to 4.8 mV) and tall R in V5-V6, frontal axis +40 deg (normal). QT 286 ms, QTc 390 ms. No bundle branch block. Versus 2022-07-04 (sinus tachycardia 115, PR 160, QRS 90, QTc 390) the tracings are essentially identical - no change.

arguments.explanation: 2025-06-23. Sinus bradycardia, rate 55 and regular (RR 1074-1118 ms). Versus the prior tracing of 2018-12-13 (sinus 66, PR 152, QRS 110, QTc 385) the QRS is now narrower and the QTc essentially unchanged (-27 ms); neither study met bundle-branch-block criteria, so no change is coded.

2023-10-08. Sinus rhythm, rate 68 (RR 862-902 ms), upright P in II/aVF, PR 136 ms. QRS 94 ms, rS in V1-V2 with tall R in V5-V6, frontal axis +44 deg (normal). Repolarisation is clearly prolonged: QT 488 ms with Bazett QTc 520 ms - above the 500 ms clinic threshold in a patient on escitalopram. No bundle branch block or AV block. Compared with 2022-11-23 (100065910: sinus 76, PR 146, QRS 92, QTc 361) the QTc has increased by about 159 ms: QTC_INCREASE_60.

2023-11-10. Sinus rhythm, rate 70 (RR 798-886 ms), upright P waves in II/III/aVF, PR 154 ms. QRS 104 ms - mildly widened but without a bundle branch block pattern (rS in V1, no broad terminal R, no broad monophasic R in I/V6). Frontal axis +52 deg (normal). Greatly prolonged repolarisation with a broad flat T wave: QT 506 ms, Bazett QTc 548 ms, well above the 500 ms threshold on citalopram 40 mg. Compared with 2020-06-17 (107149156: sinus tachycardia 132, QRS 78, QTc about 426 ms) the QTc has risen by over 100 ms: QTC_INCREASE_60.

2024-04-19. Sinus tachycardia, rate 121 (RR 476-514 ms). A low-amplitude but consistent upright P wave (0.06-0.08 mV in II/III/aVF, negative in V1) precedes each QRS with PR about 136 ms. QRS 82 ms, rS in V1-V2 with tall R in V5-V6, frontal axis +63 deg (normal). QT 286 ms, QTc 406 ms. No bundle branch block or AV block. This is the only ECG on file, so there is no prior tracing for comparison.

2024-05-21. Sinus tachycardia, rate 108 (RR 546-616 ms), upright P waves in II/aVF, PR 116 ms. QRS 92 ms with an rS in V1-V2, R/S transition at V2-V3 and a moderate R in V5-V6; frontal axis +46 deg (normal). QT about 326 ms, QTc about 438 ms. No bundle branch block or AV block. Only ECG on file - no prior study for comparison.

2024-05-23. Sinus rhythm at 98 (RR 614-628 ms, regular), upright P in II/III/aVF with a short PR of 94 ms. Narrow QRS 76 ms; tall R in I and V5 (2.0 mV) with deep rS in V1-V2 and an rS in III, giving a frontal axis of about +4 deg (normal). QT 306 ms, QTc 390 ms. No bundle branch block or AV block. Only ECG on file - no prior study for comparison.

2024-07-17. Sinus rhythm, rate 59 (RR 954-1154 ms) with an upright P in II/aVF and a prolonged PR of 208 ms - first-degree AV block. QRS is broad at 134 ms with a left bundle branch block pattern: broad monophasic R in I (peak 24 ms, no S) and in V6, deep broad QS complexes in V1-V2 and III, and delayed intrinsicoid deflection; frontal axis about -28 deg. QT 430 ms, QTc 427 ms. Compared with 2024-06-03 (103686933) the same 132 ms LBBB pattern was already present with QTc 438 ms, so no new or resolved bundle branch block and no significant QTc change; the PR has lengthened from 124 to 208 ms.

2024-09-17. Atrial fibrillation: no P waves in any lead (pre-QRS baseline flat at the noise level) and a grossly irregularly irregular ventricular response, RR 410-912 ms, mean rate 103. PR interval not measurable. QRS 86 ms with a small r and deep S in II/III/aVF and tall R in I/V5, frontal axis about -53 deg (left axis deviation). QT 316 ms, QTc 413 ms. No bundle branch block. Only ECG on file, so no prior tracing for comparison; the patient is on warfarin.

2024-10-24. Sinus bradycardia, rate 52 and very regular (RR 1144-1178 ms, CV 0.009). A low-amplitude (about 0.06 mV) but reproducible upright P wave in II/III/aVF precedes each QRS, PR about 150 ms - no fibrillatory activity despite the history of atrial fibrillation. QRS 96 ms with very tall R waves in V5-V6 (4.1/3.3 mV) and deep S in V1-V2; frontal axis +37 deg (normal). QT 436 ms, QTc 404 ms. No bundle branch block or AV block. Versus 2023-05-22 (104629882: sinus 58 with one premature beat, PR 142, QRS 92, QTc 387) there is no significant change.

2024-11-15. Atrial fibrillation: no organised P waves (pre-QRS signal at baseline, no reproducible atrial deflection across beats) with a grossly irregular ventricular response, RR 454-1148 ms, mean rate 70. PR not measurable. QRS 100 ms with terminal slurring but no complete bundle branch block pattern; tall R in I/V5-V6, deep S in V1-V2; frontal axis +30 deg (normal). QT 430 ms, QTc 466 ms. Compared with the tracing three days earlier (107873952, 2024-11-12) which showed sinus rhythm at 69 with clear P waves, PR 160 ms, QRS 86 ms and QTc 388 ms, this is NEW_AF, and the QTc has risen by about 78 ms (QTC_INCREASE_60).

2024-12-05 14:38. Sinus tachycardia, rate 122 and metronomically regular (RR 492-496 ms), small upright P waves in II/aVF, PR 124 ms. QRS has narrowed to 86 ms. Overall QRS voltage is low; lead I is net negative and aVF near isoelectric, giving a rightward/indeterminate frontal axis of roughly +163 deg (RIGHT). QT 300 ms, QTc 427 ms. Compared with the tracing from earlier the same day (106516875, 01:33) which showed a 144 ms right bundle branch block - tall broad terminal R in V1 peaking at 62 ms with wide S waves in I and V6 - the QRS is now narrow: RESOLVED_BUNDLE_BRANCH_BLOCK. QTc fell from 468 to 427 ms (less than 60 ms).

2020-06-19. Sinus rhythm, rate 76 (RR 774-804 ms), prominent upright P waves in II/III/aVF (0.21 mV) with PR 154 ms. Narrow QRS 72 ms, rS in V1 with normal precordial progression, frontal axis +66 deg (normal). QT 396 ms, QTc 447 ms. No conduction block. Compared with 2020-02-02 (109048192: sinus 75, PR 154, QRS 64, QTc 529 ms with diffuse low-amplitude T-wave inversion) the repolarisation has largely normalised: QTc fell by about 82 ms, coded QTC_DECREASE_60.

2025-02-15. Sinus rhythm, rate 74 and regular (RR 802-824 ms), P wave upright in I and II (negative in III) with PR 174 ms. QRS 90 ms with large biphasic complexes in the limb leads (I +1.25/-0.82 mV, III +1.20/-1.13 mV); net frontal axis about +37 deg (normal). QT 378 ms, QTc 420 ms. No bundle branch block or AV block. Only ECG on file - no prior study for comparison.

2025-03-09. Sinus bradycardia, rate 58 (RR 976-1082 ms), tall upright P waves in II/III/aVF (0.17 mV) with PR 110 ms. QRS 90 ms with deep rS in V1-V2 (V2 S 3.0 mV) and tall R in V5-V6; frontal axis +60 deg (normal). QT 408 ms, QTc 403 ms. No bundle branch block or AV block - a useful baseline now that haloperidol has been started. Versus the previous day (106045460, 2025-03-08: sinus 62, PR 110, QRS 92, QTc 436) there is no significant change.

2025-03-14. Sinus rhythm at 62 with an isolated premature atrial beat: RR are 956-986 ms apart from one early cycle of 548 ms followed by a 1202 ms pause. A discrete P wave (upright in I, low in II, negative in III) precedes each sinus QRS with PR 198 ms, at the upper limit of normal but not yet first-degree AV block. QRS 104 ms, tall R in I and V5 with rS in II/III/aVF; net frontal axis about -26 deg (borderline leftward but within the normal range). QT 368 ms, QTc 374 ms. No bundle branch block. No P-wave-less irregular activity - no atrial fibrillation on this tracing, although paroxysmal AF is documented. Only ECG on file - no prior study for comparison.

2025-03-19. Sinus rhythm at 102 (RR 580-594 ms, regular), upright P in II with PR 130 ms. QRS 92 ms, small R in V1 with tall R in V5-V6, frontal axis +44 deg (normal). QT 326 ms, QTc 425 ms. No bundle branch block or AV block. Versus the previous day (101016166, 2025-03-18: sinus 102, PR 128, QRS 92, QTc 421) there is no change.

2025-05-12. Sinus rhythm, rate 82 and regular (RR 710-744 ms), upright P in I/II/aVF, PR 132 ms. QRS mildly widened at 106 ms with nonspecific terminal slurring but no bundle branch block pattern (rS in V1, no broad monophasic R in I/V6, no terminal R in V1). Frontal axis about +28 deg (normal). QT 372 ms, QTc 436 ms. No AV block. Only ECG on file - no prior study for comparison.

2021-01-18. Sinus tachycardia, rate 121 and strikingly regular (RR 496-500 ms). A discrete upright P wave (0.19 mV in II, negative in V1) sits between the previous T wave and the QRS, giving PR about 175 ms. QRS 88 ms, rS in V1-V2 with tall R in V5, frontal axis +44 deg (normal). QT 276 ms, QTc 391 ms. No bundle branch block. Versus 2016-09-16 (sinus tachycardia 108, PR 176, QRS 88, QTc 397) there is no significant change.

2021-08-23 10:07. Sinus rhythm at the upper limit of normal, rate 102 (RR 586-608 ms), upright P in II/aVF, PR 138 ms. QRS 94 ms with deep rS in V1-V2 and tall R in V5-V6 (voltage suggesting LV hypertrophy), frontal axis +56 deg (normal). QT 316 ms, QTc 411 ms. No bundle branch block or AV block. Essentially identical to the tracing taken one minute earlier the same day (102910502: rate 100, PR 138, QRS 94, QTc 408) - no change.

2022-04-27. Sinus bradycardia, rate 58 with only gradual RR variation (972-1098 ms) and a small but consistent P wave (about 0.05 mV, best seen in I/aVF) before every QRS, PR 166 ms. QRS 88 ms, rS V1-V2 with tall R in V5-V6, frontal axis +25 deg (normal). Markedly prolonged repolarisation: QT 542 ms, Bazett QTc 532 ms - relevant on amiodarone plus warfarin. No bundle branch block. Compared with 2022-04-06 (100867733), which showed atrial fibrillation with no P waves and a grossly irregular response at a mean 129 bpm, organised atrial activity has returned (RESOLVED_AF) and the QTc has risen by about 96 ms (QTC_INCREASE_60).

2022-05-01. Sinus tachycardia, rate 107 (RR 542-576 ms, regular). A separate upright P wave follows the T wave in each cycle (0.18 mV in II), PR about 150 ms. QRS narrow at 68 ms, deep S in V1-V2 with tall R in V5, frontal axis +52 deg (normal). QT about 336 ms, QTc about 450 ms. No conduction block. Versus 2019-07-27 (sinus 75, PR 150, QRS 86, QTc 427) there is no significant change apart from the faster rate.

2022-07-13. Sinus tachycardia, rate 141 and regular (RR 404-454 ms, CV 0.02). A small discrete P wave (0.05 mV in II, 0.11 mV in V1) is visible after the T wave in each cycle, PR about 106 ms. QRS 84 ms with tall R in I, rS in III and very deep S in V1-V2, frontal axis about -3 deg (normal). QT about 274 ms, QTc about 420 ms. No bundle branch block. The previous tracing two days earlier (109839112, 2022-07-11) showed atrial fibrillation - absent P waves with RR 382-822 ms - so sinus rhythm has been restored: RESOLVED_AF. QTc unchanged (425 to 420 ms).

2022-07-16. Sinus rhythm, rate 91 and very regular (RR 652-666 ms), upright P waves in II/aVF with PR 158 ms. QRS 84 ms; rS in III and aVF with an isoelectric net lead II, giving a frontal axis of about -18 deg (within the normal -30 to +90 range but leftward). Prominent R in V5-V6 with deep S in V1-V2. QT 334 ms, QTc 412 ms. No bundle branch block or AV block. Versus 2021-05-16 (sinus 87, PR 136, QRS 86, QTc 396) only a modest leftward axis shift; no coded change.

2023-06-26. Sinus tachycardia, rate 112 (RR 506-572 ms). One upright P wave per cycle (0.15 mV in II, positive in III/aVF, biphasic in V1) clearly separated from the preceding T wave, PR about 170 ms - there is no sawtooth flutter activity despite the history of atrial flutter. QRS 92 ms with a very deep S in V1-V2 (up to 4.8 mV) and tall R in V5-V6, frontal axis +40 deg (normal). QT 286 ms, QTc 390 ms. No bundle branch block. Versus 2022-07-04 (sinus tachycardia 115, PR 160, QRS 90, QTc 390) the tracings are essentially identical - no change.

items.explanation: 71-year-old woman with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation (Condition I48.0) and no anticoagulant of any kind current as of 2026-09-24 (last clinic note 2026-07-10 lists only carvedilol, metoprolol and famotidine; no warfarin/DOAC order active). CHA2DS2-VASc 5 (hypertension 1, age 71 -> 1, prior cardioembolic cerebral infarction with residual hemiplegia 2, female 1); 2023 ACC/AHA/ACCP/HRS guideline recommends oral anticoagulation at this risk. Thrombocytopenia and CKD are noted and should be weighed when choosing an agent.

Amiodarone (QT watch list) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2025-11-10 (first amiodarone order for this patient; it appears newly in the current-medication list of that note). The start is on/after 9/1/2025 and before 3/1/2026, so the 9/1/2025 memo applies with a 30-day window: ECG due by 2025-12-10. ECG 106885519 was recorded 2025-11-24, 14 days after the start, so the requirement was met.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch list) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-02-12 (first escitalopram order; newly listed in that note). Started before 3/1/2026, so the 9/1/2025 memo 30-day window applies: ECG due by 2026-03-14. ECG 101538691 was recorded 2026-03-08, 24 days after the start, within the window - requirement met (QTc 437 ms, acceptable).

Citalopram 40 mg daily (QT watch list) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-03-02 (first citalopram order; newly listed in that note). Start is on/after 3/1/2026, so the revised memo applies with a 14-day window: ECG due by 2026-03-16. ECG 104882441 was recorded at the 2026-03-07 clinic visit, 5 days after the start - requirement met (QTc 381 ms).

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch list) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-04-10 (first escitalopram order; newly listed in that note). Start on/after 3/1/2026, so a 14-day window applies: ECG due by 2026-04-24. The only ECG on file (107859369) was recorded 2026-04-29, five days after the deadline, so nothing satisfied the requirement within the required time and the due date has passed - overdue.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch list) was restarted at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-08-01 - it appears newly in that note current-medication list and the only prior exposure was a brief inpatient surgical course 2025-12-30 to 2026-01-01, seven months earlier. Start on/after 3/1/2026, so a 14-day window applies: ECG due by 2026-08-15. No ECG has been recorded since 2025-12-25 (106035722) and the due date has passed - overdue.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch list) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-08-10 (newly listed in that note; no prior escitalopram). Start on/after 3/1/2026, so a 14-day window applies: ECG due by 2026-08-24. The nurse telephone note of 2026-08-25 records that the patient had an ECG at Northside Urgent Care on 8/18/2026 - inside the window - and that the report was requested by fax but not yet received. That outside tracing could have satisfied the requirement but it is not in the chart, so completion cannot be determined; the report should be chased.

Haloperidol 2 mg twice daily (QT watch list) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-09-15 (newly listed in that note; no prior haloperidol order). Start on/after 3/1/2026, so a 14-day window applies: ECG due by 2026-09-29. No ECG has been obtained since 2025-03-09, but as of the 2026-09-24 evaluation the requirement is not yet due.

Warfarin dose change made by a Cardiology Clinic clinician (Dr. Paul Kessler) in the 2026-09-01 clinic note: INR today 1.6, subtherapeutic. Increase warfarin to 7.5 mg daily; recheck INR. Under the 3/1/2026 memo an INR is required within 7 days, i.e. by 2026-09-08. INR 2.3 was resulted on 2026-09-05, four days after the change - requirement met.

Warfarin dose change made by a clinic pharmacist acting under the anticoagulation standing order (L. Nguyen, PharmD, 2026-09-10 anticoagulation clinic telephone note): home INR 3.4, warfarin decreased from 5 mg to 4 mg daily per protocol. The 3/1/2026 memo requires an INR within 7 days, i.e. by 2026-09-17. The home INR 3.4 is the result that prompted the change, not a follow-up, and no INR has been resulted since 2026-08-22 (2.6). The due date has passed with no confirmatory INR - overdue.

71-year-old man with atrial fibrillation (Condition ICD-9 427.31, carried in every cardiology clinic note through 2026-07-28) and no anticoagulant current: the only active outpatient order is tamsulosin (2026-07-28 to 2027-01-01) and the 2026-07-28 note lists tamsulosin alone. CHA2DS2-VASc 3 (hypertension 1, age 71 -> 1, vascular disease 1 - coronary atherosclerosis of native coronary artery with three-vessel CABG plus LIMA graft on 2025-08-22). Score >=2 in a man: guideline recommends oral anticoagulation. Note the documented peri-procedural haemorrhage (ICD-9 998.11) from that admission should be weighed at review.

Apixaban 5 mg twice daily is current (order 2026-08-20 through 2026-12-28, and the 2026-08-20 clinic note lists apixaban under Continue current regimen). However the 2026-08-12 summary-of-episode note documents an outside admission 8/2-8/5/2026 for upper GI bleeding from a duodenal ulcer, haemoglobin nadir 6.9 g/dL, 2 units transfused, with apixaban HELD at discharge pending cardiology review. The anticoagulant was restarted without that review being documented, and the patient is also on aspirin 81 mg and clopidogrel 75 mg, compounding bleeding risk. Needs prescriber review before continuing.

Two different oral anticoagulants are simultaneously current: apixaban 5 mg twice daily (order 2026-07-15 to 2026-12-26) and rivaroxaban 20 mg daily (order 2026-07-15 to 2026-12-25). The 2026-07-15 cardiology note states the intention was to switch FROM rivaroxaban TO apixaban for insurance coverage, but the rivaroxaban order was never stopped and the same note still lists both agents as current medications. Overlapping factor Xa inhibitors greatly increase bleeding risk, particularly with concurrent CLL; one order must be discontinued.

The 2026-06-10 cardiology clinic note states ECG obtained today: normal sinus rhythm, rate 72. Both ECGs recorded that day (107914094 at 17:13 and 103088543 at 19:36) show atrial fibrillation with a rapid, grossly irregular ventricular response: no P waves at all in any lead, RR intervals ranging 346-718 ms (mean rate 134-136 bpm). The documented rhythm and rate are contradicted by the same-day tracings, and a rate of ~135 in AF on warfarin needs rate-control review.

95-year-old woman on amiodarone 200 mg daily (QT watch list), order current 2026-08-22 to 2027-01-05. Her most recent ECG (101515306, 2022-04-27) shows sinus rhythm at 58 bpm with QT 542 ms and Bazett QTc 532 ms, i.e. >=500 ms, which the 2025-01-15 QT monitoring memo says requires prescriber review. Most recent electrolytes (2026-02-14): potassium 4.1 mEq/L, magnesium 1.8 mg/dL (low-normal). She is also on warfarin, which amiodarone potentiates. No ECG since 2022 despite continued amiodarone.

56-year-old man on escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch list), order current 2026-04-23 to 2027-01-02. Most recent ECG (108018814, 2023-10-08) is sinus rhythm at 68 bpm with QT 488 ms and Bazett QTc 520 ms, >=500 ms, so the 2025-01-15 QT monitoring memo requires prescriber review. This is a marked increase from his previous ECG (100065910, 2022-11-23, QTc 361 ms). The 2024-05-14 note that started escitalopram recorded the 10/8/2023 ECG as QT acceptable, which the measured QTc does not support. Most recent electrolytes (2025-08-23): potassium 4.1 mEq/L, magnesium 2.1 mg/dL.

35-year-old woman on citalopram 40 mg daily (QT watch list; 40 mg exceeds the 20 mg maximum advised in patients at QT risk), order current 2026-05-29 to 2026-12-25. Most recent ECG (104821039, 2023-11-10) shows sinus rhythm at 70 bpm, QT 506 ms, Bazett QTc 548 ms, well above the 500 ms threshold in the 2025-01-15 QT monitoring memo, and up from QTc ~426 ms on the previous tracing (107149156, 2020-06-17). Most recent potassium 4.5 mEq/L (2026-01-21) and magnesium 2.1 mg/dL (2023-12-01). Also on levothyroxine. Prescriber review of dose and a repeat ECG are needed.

79-year-old man with atrial fibrillation on amiodarone 200 mg daily (QT watch list), order current 2026-07-29 to 2027-01-05, plus warfarin. Most recent ECG (106885519, 2025-11-24) shows sinus rhythm at 62 bpm with QT 520 ms and Bazett QTc 528 ms, >=500 ms, which the 2025-01-15 QT monitoring memo says requires prescriber review; this is a rise of ~78 ms from the previous tracing (108780865, 2025-06-07, QTc 450 ms) after amiodarone was started on 2025-11-10. Most recent electrolytes (2026-04-20): potassium 4.4 mEq/L, magnesium 2.2 mg/dL.

interpretations.explanation: 2019-01-13. Sinus bradycardia, rate 53 (RR 1112-1170 ms, regular), upright consistent P waves in II/aVF preceded each QRS with PR 138 ms. QRS 94 ms with a qR pattern in I/V5-V6 and deep S in III/aVF; frontal axis about -14 deg (normal). QT 382 ms, Bazett QTc 358 ms. No bundle branch block or AV block. Versus the prior tracing of 2018-12-13 (sinus 66, PR 152, QRS 110, QTc 385) the QRS is now narrower and the QTc essentially unchanged (-27 ms); neither study met bundle-branch-block criteria, so no change is coded.

2023-10-08. Sinus rhythm, rate 68 (RR 862-902 ms), upright P in II/aVF, PR 136 ms. QRS 94 ms, rS in V1-V2 with tall R in V5-V6, frontal axis +44 deg (normal). Repolarisation is clearly prolonged: QT 488 ms with Bazett QTc 520 ms - above the 500 ms clinic threshold in a patient on escitalopram. No bundle branch block or AV block. Compared with 2022-11-23 (100065910: sinus 76, PR 146, QRS 92, QTc 361) the QTc has increased by about 159 ms: QTC_INCREASE_60.

2023-11-10. Sinus rhythm, rate 70 (RR 798-886 ms), upright P waves in II/III/aVF, PR 154 ms. QRS 104 ms - mildly widened but without a bundle branch block pattern (rS in V1, no broad terminal R, no broad monophasic R in I/V6). Frontal axis +52 deg (normal). Greatly prolonged repolarisation with a broad flat T wave: QT 506 ms, Bazett QTc 548 ms, well above the 500 ms threshold on citalopram 40 mg. Compared with 2020-06-17 (107149156: sinus tachycardia 132, QRS 78, QTc about 426 ms) the QTc has risen by over 100 ms: QTC_INCREASE_60.

2024-04-19. Sinus tachycardia, rate 121 (RR 476-514 ms). A low-amplitude but consistent upright P wave (0.06-0.08 mV in II/III/aVF, negative in V1) precedes each QRS with PR about 136 ms. QRS 82 ms, rS in V1-V2 with tall R in V5-V6, frontal axis +63 deg (normal). QT 286 ms, QTc 406 ms. No bundle branch block or AV block. This is the only ECG on file, so there is no prior tracing for comparison.

2024-05-21. Sinus tachycardia, rate 108 (RR 546-616 ms), upright P waves in II/aVF, PR 116 ms. QRS 92 ms with an rS in V1-V2, R/S transition at V2-V3 and a moderate R in V5-V6; frontal axis +46 deg (normal). QT about 326 ms, QTc about 438 ms. No bundle branch block or AV block. Only ECG on file - no prior study for comparison.

2024-05-23. Sinus rhythm at 98 (RR 614-628 ms, regular), upright P in II/III/aVF with a short PR of 94 ms. Narrow QRS 76 ms; tall R in I and V5 (2.0 mV) with deep rS in V1-V2 and an rS in III, giving a frontal axis of about +4 deg (normal). QT 306 ms, QTc 390 ms. No bundle branch block or AV block. Only ECG on file - no prior study for comparison.

2024-07-17. Sinus rhythm, rate 59 (RR 954-1154 ms) with an upright P in II/aVF and a prolonged PR of 208 ms - first-degree AV block. QRS is broad at 134 ms with a left bundle branch block pattern: broad monophasic R in I (peak 24 ms, no S) and in V6, deep broad QS complexes in V1-V2 and III, and delayed intrinsicoid deflection; frontal axis about -28 deg. QT 430 ms, QTc 427 ms. Compared with 2024-06-03 (103686933) the same 132 ms LBBB pattern was already present with QTc 438 ms, so no new or resolved bundle branch block and no significant QTc change; the PR has lengthened from 124 to 208 ms.

2024-09-17. Atrial fibrillation: no P waves in any lead (pre-QRS baseline flat at the noise level) and a grossly irregularly irregular ventricular response, RR 410-912 ms, mean rate 103. PR interval not measurable. QRS 86 ms with a small r and deep S in II/III/aVF and tall R in I/V5, frontal axis about -53 deg (left axis deviation). QT 316 ms, QTc 413 ms. No bundle branch block. Only ECG on file, so no prior tracing for comparison; the patient is on warfarin.

2024-10-24. Sinus bradycardia, rate 52 and very regular (RR 1144-1178 ms, CV 0.009). A low-amplitude (about 0.06 mV) but reproducible upright P wave in II/III/aVF precedes each QRS, PR about 150 ms - no fibrillatory activity despite the history of atrial fibrillation. QRS 96 ms with very tall R waves in V5-V6 (4.1/3.3 mV) and deep S in V1-V2; frontal axis +37 deg (normal). QT 436 ms, QTc 404 ms. No bundle branch block or AV block. Versus 2023-05-22 (104629882: sinus 58 with one premature beat, PR 142, QRS 92, QTc 387) there is no significant change.

2024-11-15. Atrial fibrillation: no organised P waves (pre-QRS signal at baseline, no reproducible atrial deflection across beats) with a grossly irregular ventricular response, RR 454-1148 ms, mean rate 70. PR not measurable. QRS 100 ms with terminal slurring but no complete bundle branch block pattern; tall R in I/V5-V6, deep S in V1-V2; frontal axis +30 deg (normal). QT 430 ms, QTc 466 ms. Compared with the tracing three days earlier (107873952, 2024-11-12) which showed sinus rhythm at 69 with clear P waves, PR 160 ms, QRS 86 ms and QTc 388 ms, this is NEW_AF, and the QTc has risen by about 78 ms (QTC_INCREASE_60).

2024-12-05 14:38. Sinus tachycardia, rate 122 and metronomically regular (RR 492-496 ms), small upright P waves in II/aVF, PR 124 ms. QRS has narrowed to 86 ms. Overall QRS voltage is low; lead I is net negative and aVF near isoelectric, giving a rightward/indeterminate frontal axis of roughly +163 deg (RIGHT). QT 300 ms, QTc 427 ms. Compared with the tracing from earlier the same day (106516875, 01:33) which showed a 144 ms right bundle branch block - tall broad terminal R in V1 peaking at 62 ms with wide S waves in I and V6 - the QRS is now narrow: RESOLVED_BUNDLE_BRANCH_BLOCK. QTc fell from 468 to 427 ms (less than 60 ms).

2020-06-19. Sinus rhythm, rate 76 (RR 774-804 ms), prominent upright P waves in II/III/aVF (0.21 mV) with PR 154 ms. Narrow QRS 72 ms, rS in V1 with normal precordial progression, frontal axis +66 deg (normal). QT 396 ms, QTc 447 ms. No conduction block. Compared with 2020-02-02 (109048192: sinus 75, PR 154, QRS 64, QTc 529 ms with diffuse low-amplitude T-wave inversion) the repolarisation has largely normalised: QTc fell by about 82 ms, coded QTC_DECREASE_60.

2025-02-15. Sinus rhythm, rate 74 and regular (RR 802-824 ms), P wave upright in I and II (negative in III) with PR 174 ms. QRS 90 ms with large biphasic complexes in the limb leads (I +1.25/-0.82 mV, III +1.20/-1.13 mV); net frontal axis about +37 deg (normal). QT 378 ms, QTc 420 ms. No bundle branch block or AV block. Only ECG on file - no prior study for comparison.

2025-03-09. Sinus bradycardia, rate 58 (RR 976-1082 ms), tall upright P waves in II/III/aVF (0.17 mV) with PR 110 ms. QRS 90 ms with deep rS in V1-V2 (V2 S 3.0 mV) and tall R in V5-V6; frontal axis +60 deg (normal). QT 408 ms, QTc 403 ms. No bundle branch block or AV block - a useful baseline now that haloperidol has been started. Versus the previous day (106045460, 2025-03-08: sinus 62, PR 110, QRS 92, QTc 436) there is no significant change.

2025-03-14. Sinus rhythm at 62 with an isolated premature atrial beat: RR are 956-986 ms apart from one early cycle of 548 ms followed by a 1202 ms pause. A discrete P wave (upright in I, low in II, negative in III) precedes each sinus QRS with PR 198 ms, at the upper limit of normal but not yet first-degree AV block. QRS 104 ms, tall R in I and V5 with rS in II/III/aVF; net frontal axis about -26 deg (borderline leftward but within the normal range). QT 368 ms, QTc 374 ms. No bundle branch block. No P-wave-less irregular activity - no atrial fibrillation on this tracing, although paroxysmal AF is documented. Only ECG on file - no prior study for comparison.

2025-03-19. Sinus rhythm at 102 (RR 580-594 ms, regular), upright P in II with PR 130 ms. QRS 92 ms, small R in V1 with tall R in V5-V6, frontal axis +44 deg (normal). QT 326 ms, QTc 425 ms. No bundle branch block or AV block. Versus the previous day (101016166, 2025-03-18: sinus 102, PR 128, QRS 92, QTc 421) there is no change.

2025-05-12. Sinus rhythm, rate 82 and regular (RR 710-744 ms), upright P in I/II/aVF, PR 132 ms. QRS mildly widened at 106 ms with nonspecific terminal slurring but no bundle branch block pattern (rS in V1, no broad monophasic R in I/V6, no terminal R in V1). Frontal axis about +28 deg (normal). QT 372 ms, QTc 436 ms. No AV block. Only ECG on file - no prior study for comparison.

2025-06-23. Sinus bradycardia, rate 55 and regular (RR 1074-1118 ms). An upright P wave (0.12 mV in II, positive in III/aVF) begins about 224 ms before the QRS - PR 224 ms, i.e. first-degree AV block. QRS 88 ms with large biphasic precordial complexes (V2 +1.76/-1.53 mV) and tall R in V5 (2.8 mV); frontal axis about +34 deg (normal). QT 402 ms, QTc 383 ms. No bundle branch block. Versus 2024-11-30 (103042067: sinus 51, PR 188 ms, QRS 88, QTc 366) the PR interval has lengthened further; no coded change category applies.

2025-07-15. Sinus tachycardia, rate 104 (RR 570-586 ms, regular), upright P in I/II with PR 112 ms. QRS 100 ms with an rS in V1-V2 and tall R in I; frontal axis about +19 deg (normal). QT about 330 ms, QTc about 434 ms. No bundle branch block or AV block. Compared with 2025-06-20 (100698634: regular narrow-complex tachycardia at 147 with the P wave buried in the preceding T wave, QRS 84 ms, QT about 277 ms, QTc about 434 ms) the rate has slowed with no change in QTc or conduction.

2021-01-18. Sinus tachycardia, rate 121 and strikingly regular (RR 496-500 ms). A discrete upright P wave (0.19 mV in II, negative in V1) sits between the previous T wave and the QRS, giving PR about 175 ms. QRS 88 ms, rS in V1-V2 with tall R in V5, frontal axis +44 deg (normal). QT 276 ms, QTc 391 ms. No bundle branch block. Versus 2016-09-16 (sinus tachycardia 108, PR 176, QRS 88, QTc 397) there is no significant change.

2021-08-23 10:07. Sinus rhythm at the upper limit of normal, rate 102 (RR 586-608 ms), upright P in II/aVF, PR 138 ms. QRS 94 ms with deep rS in V1-V2 and tall R in V5-V6 (voltage suggesting LV hypertrophy), frontal axis +56 deg (normal). QT 316 ms, QTc 411 ms. No bundle branch block or AV block. Essentially identical to the tracing taken one minute earlier the same day (102910502: rate 100, PR 138, QRS 94, QTc 408) - no change.

2022-04-27. Sinus bradycardia, rate 58 with only gradual RR variation (972-1098 ms) and a small but consistent P wave (about 0.05 mV, best seen in I/aVF) before every QRS, PR 166 ms. QRS 88 ms, rS V1-V2 with tall R in V5-V6, frontal axis +25 deg (normal). Markedly prolonged repolarisation: QT 542 ms, Bazett QTc 532 ms - relevant on amiodarone plus warfarin. No bundle branch block. Compared with 2022-04-06 (100867733), which showed atrial fibrillation with no P waves and a grossly irregular response at a mean 129 bpm, organised atrial activity has returned (RESOLVED_AF) and the QTc has risen by about 96 ms (QTC_INCREASE_60).

2022-05-01. Sinus tachycardia, rate 107 (RR 542-576 ms, regular). A separate upright P wave follows the T wave in each cycle (0.18 mV in II), PR about 150 ms. QRS narrow at 68 ms, deep S in V1-V2 with tall R in V5, frontal axis +52 deg (normal). QT about 336 ms, QTc about 450 ms. No conduction block. Versus 2019-07-27 (sinus 75, PR 150, QRS 86, QTc 427) there is no significant change apart from the faster rate.

2022-07-13. Sinus tachycardia, rate 141 and regular (RR 404-454 ms, CV 0.02). A small discrete P wave (0.05 mV in II, 0.11 mV in V1) is visible after the T wave in each cycle, PR about 106 ms. QRS 84 ms with tall R in I, rS in III and very deep S in V1-V2, frontal axis about -3 deg (normal). QT about 274 ms, QTc about 420 ms. No bundle branch block. The previous tracing two days earlier (109839112, 2022-07-11) showed atrial fibrillation - absent P waves with RR 382-822 ms - so sinus rhythm has been restored: RESOLVED_AF. QTc unchanged (425 to 420 ms).

2022-07-16. Sinus rhythm, rate 91 and very regular (RR 652-666 ms), upright P waves in II/aVF with PR 158 ms. QRS 84 ms; rS in III and aVF with an isoelectric net lead II, giving a frontal axis of about -18 deg (within the normal -30 to +90 range but leftward). Prominent R in V5-V6 with deep S in V1-V2. QT 334 ms, QTc 412 ms. No bundle branch block or AV block. Versus 2021-05-16 (sinus 87, PR 136, QRS 86, QTc 396) only a modest leftward axis shift; no coded change.

2023-06-26. Sinus tachycardia, rate 112 (RR 506-572 ms). One upright P wave per cycle (0.15 mV in II, positive in III/aVF, biphasic in V1) clearly separated from the preceding T wave, PR about 170 ms - there is no sawtooth flutter activity despite the history of atrial flutter. QRS 92 ms with a very deep S in V1-V2 (up to 4.8 mV) and tall R in V5-V6, frontal axis +40 deg (normal). QT 286 ms, QTc 390 ms. No bundle branch block. Versus 2022-07-04 (sinus tachycardia 115, PR 160, QRS 90, QTc 390) the tracings are essentially identical - no change.

2024-11-15. Nguyen, PharmD, 2026-09-10 anticoagulation clinic telephone note): home INR 3.4, warfarin decreased from 5 mg to 4 mg daily per protocol. 71-year-old man with atrial fibrillation (Condition ICD-9 427.31, carried in every cardiology clinic note through 2026-07-28) and no anticoagulant current: the only active outpatient order is tamsulosin (2026-07-28 to 2027-01-01) and the 2026-07-28 note lists tamsulosin alone. CHA2DS2-VASc 3 (hypertension 1, age 71 -> 1, vascular disease 1 - coronary atherosclerosis of native coronary artery with three-vessel CABG plus LIMA graft on 2025-08-22). Score >=2 in a man: guideline recommends oral anticoagulation. Note the documented peri-procedural haemorrhage (ICD-9 998.11) from that admission should be weighed at review.

Apixaban 5 mg twice daily is current (order 2026-08-20 through 2026-12-28, and the 2026-08-20 clinic note lists apixaban under Continue current regimen). The anticoagulant was restarted without that review being documented, and the patient is also on aspirin 81 mg and clopidogrel 75 mg, compounding bleeding risk. Needs prescriber review before continuing.

Two different oral anticoagulants are simultaneously current: apixaban 5 mg twice daily (order 2026-07-15 to 2026-12-26) and rivaroxaban 20 mg daily (order 2026-07-15 to 2026-12-25). The 2026-07-15 cardiology note states the intention was to switch FROM rivaroxaban TO apixaban for insurance coverage, but the rivaroxaban order was never stopped and the same note still lists both agents as current medications. Overlapping factor Xa inhibitors greatly increase bleeding risk, particularly with concurrent CLL; one order must be discontinued.

A repeat tracing with correct limb-lead placement would be worthwhile. Only ECG on file - no prior study for comparison.
